Senses.Explanation: The bodhisattva precepts are a named class of precepts that the records describe as received, conferred, and kept. Zhuanyu Guanheng says that one who keeps them enters the bodhisattva rank. Yongming Yanshou distinguishes this precept class while defining it through contemplation of mind rather than an external object. Shanhui Huan's biography records that receiving these precepts led him to compare their demands with the monastic precepts he had already received. Yushan Shangsi's record marks their formal completion, while Weilin Daopei raises his late teacher Yongjue Yuanxian's direct question asking what the bodhisattva precepts are. These uses retain a hard rule and formal reception or conferral, even where masters state their basis in mind.
Senses.Note: The disciple-title, reception event, rule-body, and direct-question uses name the same institutional precept class; grammatical differences do not require separate senses.
